What Is Ecosystem-Led Growth?

Explainerlowob research

By lowob · 17 November 2026 · 5-minute read · Distribution

In short: Ecosystem-led growth (ELG) is a go-to-market approach in which a company uses its partners, and the customers it shares with them, to find, win and keep business. It differs from partner-led growth in one main way: the partner does not have to resell anything. The partner's customer overlap, relationships and product integrations help the company's own sellers. The term was popularised by account-mapping vendors, so its most quoted figures are vendor data and should be read that way.

Key points

  • Crossbeam, an account-mapping vendor, defines ELG as the go-to-market motion that focuses on partner ecosystems as the main way to attract, convert and grow customers.
  • Forrester's 2022 Buyers' Journey Survey of more than 10,000 B2B purchase influencers found nearly 70% had bought through an indirect route or partner in the previous 12 months.
  • Crossbeam's network data for October 2024 showed an average win-rate lift of 11.7% on deals with partners involved, and a 1% drop in one enterprise group.
  • In a 2023 Crossbeam and Pavilion survey of 425+ go-to-market leaders, 48% of sales leaders named ELG and co-selling as their main focus of the past year.
  • The evidence is mostly correlation. A firm learns whether partners move its deals only by recording each partner touch and its outcome.

What ecosystem-led growth means

A company's ecosystem is the set of other firms that sell to, integrate with or advise the same customers. ELG treats that set as a source of commercial signal. Before calling an account, a seller checks which partners already work there.

The core technique is account mapping: two companies compare customer and prospect lists to find where they overlap. Crossbeam lists it as its flagship capability, described as finding account overlaps with partners. The overlap then drives three plays: a warm introduction to a prospect, a joint approach to a shared prospect, and support for an existing customer who uses both products.

Partner-led growthEcosystem-led growthCo-selling with a platform
Who sellsThe partner sells or refersYour sellers, helped by partnersBoth sales teams on a shared deal
What the partner contributesDistribution and often deliveryIntroductions, account insight, integration proofAccess to the platform's customers and contracts
Main dataPartner-sourced pipelineAccount overlap and partner touchesCo-sell registrations and marketplace transactions

Product-Led vs Sales-Led vs Partner-Led Growth argues that a company should choose one primary motion. ELG fits that view. It is usually a support layer on a sales-led or product-led motion, not a fourth motion of its own.

Why it matters for a commercial team

Buyers already buy through partners

Forrester's 2023 data snapshot called partner purchasing an "undeniable indication" of the role partners play. Its 2025 survey of partner ecosystem and channel marketing leaders found 67% planned for indirect revenue to grow above or significantly above the previous year. Two-thirds expected the same of partner-influenced revenue. For a mid-size firm, the question is less whether partners touch its deals than whether it knows which ones.

The numbers need careful reading

Crossbeam's November 2024 analysis of its own network found an average win-rate lift of 11.7% when partners were involved. The lift was 37.1% for companies with more than 50 connected partners and 9.4% for those with one to five. One group, enterprise companies with five to ten partners, saw win rates fall by 1%. The article does not say whether lift is relative or in percentage points, and it describes correlation. Companies that invest in partners may simply be better run.

Crossbeam's ELG page also quotes larger figures, such as deals 53% more likely to close, without a stated sample or date. Treat those as marketing claims.

Partners touching a deal is an observation. Partners changing the outcome is a finding, and only your own record can show it.

How to start

A mid-size firm does not need a large partner programme to test ELG. It needs a few partners with real customer overlap and a way to record what happens.

StepWhat to doWhat to record
Choose partnersPick three whose customers match your ideal customer profileWhy each partner was chosen
Agree the dataWrite down which fields each side shares and for what useThe signed data terms
Map accountsFind shared customers and shared open prospectsOverlap count by segment
Run one playAsk for introductions on ten shared prospectsEach request, its owner and its expected outcome
CompareAfter a quarter, compare win rate and cycle length with similar deals without a partner touchThe outcome, written back to each deal

The comparison is the step most programmes skip. Without it, partner influence becomes a field sellers fill in after the deal closes.

In lowob's model the mapping tool is wiring: rent it. The record of which introduction was asked for, by whom, with what expected result, is yours to own. An agent can scan overlap and draft introduction requests at autonomy level 2. A person approves each one, because the partner relationship is the asset at risk.

lowob takeaways

  • ELG uses overlap, not resale. Partners help your sellers find and win accounts they already know.
  • It supports a primary motion. Treat it as a layer on sales-led or product-led growth.
  • Most figures are vendor data. Read win-rate lifts as correlation until your own record says otherwise.
  • Record every partner touch. The outcome against each introduction is what proves the effect.

Common questions

What is the difference between ecosystem-led growth and partner-led growth?

In partner-led growth the partner sells, refers or delivers. In ecosystem-led growth the company's own team uses partners' customer overlap and relationships to support its deals.

What is account mapping?

Comparing customer and prospect lists with a partner to find shared accounts, usually through a tool that limits what each side can see.

Who coined ecosystem-led growth?

The term has been promoted mainly by Crossbeam, an account-mapping vendor, and by a book of the same name by Bob Moore featured on its site.

Does ecosystem-led growth work for small companies?

It can, with a few well-matched partners. Crossbeam's own data showed smaller lifts for companies with few connected partners, so measure before scaling.

Sources and notes

  • Crossbeam, What is Ecosystem-Led Growth (ELG)?, accessed November 2026. Vendor page; headline statistics have no stated sample or date.
  • Crossbeam ELG Insider, New data: involving partners in deals increases win rate for nearly every ecosystem size and type, 8 November 2024. Vendor analysis of its own network; correlation, sample sizes not given.
  • Crossbeam and Pavilion, New Report: 89% of Business Leaders Questioning Existing GTM Models, 16 November 2023. Vendor-sponsored survey of 425+ leaders, 77% at B2B SaaS firms.
  • Forrester, B2B Buyer Preferences Offer An Undeniable Indicator Of Partner Ecosystem Importance, 20 July 2023. Analyst summary page; full report behind paywall.
  • Forrester, Continued Growth In Scale And Complexity: The State Of Partner Ecosystems In 2025, 7 July 2025. Analyst blog; survey sample not stated, figures are plans not results.

Next Move

Ask your three closest partners for a list of shared customers, under written data terms, and count the overlap with your open pipeline. If the overlap is under a handful of deals, ELG is not yet your lever; if it is larger, run one introduction play for a quarter and record the outcomes.
